label: paragraph_title
text: TOKYO OLYMPIC.

label: text
text: 1929 MEET TO BE IN

label: text
text: Future Far Eastern Olympic Games will be held in September, not in May as at present, according to a decision reached at an informal conference between the Japanese and the Chinese athletes on their survival in Manila.

label: text
text: It was also decided that the 1927 Olympic Games should be held in Peking or Shanghai, and that the 1929 meet should be staged in Tokyo. After that year it was suggested that the Games should be held once in every four years, not in alternate years as at present and that therefore the first meet after the coming into force of this new rule should be held in 1933 in Manila.

label: text
text:
Regarding the coming Games the conference considered the proposal offered by the Filipino athletes and agreed to assign to the Pentathlon and Decation contests one unit in the championship calculations, as distinct from other land games, to play the base-ball matches on the two-round system, but volleyball and basketball matches on the one-round system, and to make the fancy-diving contest an open event.
The Japanese delegates offered the proposal that, from the next Olympic Games land events should constitute three units towards the championship, namely track events one, field events one, and mixed events one. The Chinese delegates on the other hand counter-proposed the inclusion of the relays in the mixed contests, constituting one unit for the championship. No decision was reached on this point.

label: text
text: In his latest article, in the "Daily News," "continuing his comments on the English team's Australian tour," J. B. Hobbs says: "Years ago I published a book, 'How to Make a Century,' which is now out of print. My own copy was sold on behalf of a charity fund, and I could not obtain another. On the third morning of the first test, at Sydney, however, a parcel was delivered at our hotel, addressed to me. It was a copy of my book, and inside the cover the anonymous donor had written: 'Study it well, J.B. You'll need it.' It seemed to be a direct challenge, and certainly put me on my mettle, for I made 115. I sincerely thank the donor of the book and hope that he reads this story.

label: text
text: ENGLAND'S TENNIS HORES.

label: text
text: Will England's "four Joans" eventually regain England's tennis supremacy?

label: text
text: Miss Reid-Thomas possessed the best woman's fore-arm drive in the country, Miss Ridley, who vanquished Miss Reid-Thomas at Rochampton, was probably the better all rounder of the two, and was developing a Patterson-like over-

label: text
text:
That question is asked by Mrs. Lambert-Chambers in an article in the 'Standard.' She says that at least half a dozen girls are showing distinct possibilities of winning the international championship.
There was little to choose between Joan Lycett, Joan Fry, Joan Reid-Thomas, and Joan Ridley. She considered Miss Fry, after Miss McKane, the most consistent player of the younger generation in England. Naturally Miss McKane was 'every' body's first choice, but Miss Fry had plenty of pluck and determination. She also possessed a perfect match temperament. Her victory over Miss McKane was well deserved.
Mrs. Lycett had improved tremendously; and had added a useful "job" to her repertoire of strokes.

label: text
text: Miss Colyer's poor ground shots were now spoiling her play in singles matches. A newcomer in Miss Peggy Saunders, though at present failing at critical moments, had the greatest chance of winning the highest honours.

label: text
text: The best team for the projected tour to America should include Misses McKane, Colyer Saunders, Harvey, and the "four Joans."

DEMPSEY AND KEARNS
PART.

label: text
text: Before leaving on a belated honeymoon, Jack Dempsey announced the end of his business partnership with Jack Kearns. They jointly own £200,000 worth of Los Angeles real estate, which will be sold during the next few months in order to divide the proceeds.

label: text
text:
Dempsey declared that he is unwilling to fight again under a contract which gives Rearns an equal share with himself.
“It is obvious, even to the non-medical, that the physical factor must play an important part in the general health when these strenuous sports, such as football and rowing, are encouraged. It is possible to overwork young horses and it is just as possible to overwork young boys, without any apparent sign of strain; but the trainers of young horses take great care not to overload them in their work.”

label: text
text: "Another aspect of these strenuous school sports, and" very serious one, is the excessive amount of publicity bestowed upon the young heroes. Our boys should not be placed in the position of national heroes, like bullfighters."

label: text
text: "Athleticism has run mad in the Greater Public Schools," he declared. "Indeed, so strong is the cult of athleticism in those schools that it seems to me that the schools are using the prowess of their boys as an advertisement." The worst thing that could happen to a schoolboy nowadays is to show a great talent for athletics. His devotion to school football and rowing is liable to interfere with the development of his character." We are rightly keen on athletics, but there is a wrong sense of perspective applied to them.

label: paragraph_title
text: ATHLETICISM RUN MAD

label: text
text: Dr. H. M. Moran, of Sydney who captained the Wallabies' football team in England, has strong views, quite apart from the medical aspect, on the question of school athletics.

label: paragraph_title
text: MASSAGE

label: text
text: Golfers don't as a rule go in for muscle massage and such artificial aids to physiological stimulation, as footballers, tennis players, and sportsmen in other strenuous fields. Maybe they are making a mistake in not doing so. At any rate, the inside history of V.T. England's victory in the recent Blackheath championship makes it appear so. Between rounds England's honorary trainer, Duncan MacMillan, got to work on his charge and pummelled embrocation into him for three-quarters of an hour—right up to within a few minutes of starting. The effect was magical, England played inspired golf, reached the turn-in 33, and finished the round one stroke over the course record, 73. His opponent was beaten, as much by surprise at the vigour of his adversary as by the par variety of his golf.
